title: Customer Reference Program (Case Studies + Reference Calls) — Project Plan (Draft)
content:
Doc purpose
- Working plan to recruit 3–5 design partners for (1) public case studies and (2) scheduled reference calls.
- Goal is a repeatable operating model: intake → qualify → recruit → capture proof → legal approval → publish → reference-call ops.

Success criteria (program-level)
- 3–5 customers signed and approved for PUBLIC case studies (web + PDF).
- Internal reference ops live: request intake form + routing + SLA + prep docs.
- Sales enablement shipped: talk track + discovery questions + “how to request a reference” one-pager.
- Measurement: # case studies published, # reference calls completed, influenced pipeline tracking in HubSpot.

Non-goals / guardrails
- No “hero” claims without measurement notes and validation owner.
- Avoid security-sensitive architecture details (anything that triggers customer security review). Use approved language only.
- Do not imply features outside current SLAs/product behavior.

Stakeholders + roles (working)
- Exec sponsor: Jordan Blake (CRO) — unblock + escalation
- Program owner: Camila Reyes (VP Marketing) — timeline, approvals, final go/no-go for publication
- Messaging lead: Soojin Lee (Dir Product Marketing) — narrative + positioning, claim phrasing
- Writer/interviewer: Ethan Wallace — interviews, drafts, quotes
- Web rollout: Ben Carter (Growth) — case studies page + publish steps + SEO basics
- Marketing ops/tracking: Tyler Benson — project tracker hygiene, Drive asset organization
- CRM ops/reporting: Isabelle Laurent — HubSpot fields + automation, reporting
- CS owner: Jasmine Liu — ensures we don’t overdraw on customer goodwill
- CS program: Rachel Kim — reference readiness, call boundaries, scheduling windows
- CSM execution: Miguel Santos — champion mgmt, prep, post-call follow-up
- SE lead: Markus Klein — technical validation, diagrams/architecture sanity checks
- Solutions Architect: Simran Kaur — metrics methodology review + deployment accuracy
- Metrics/telemetry: Logan Wright + Sana Farid — data sources, measurement windows, “notes” section that can be reproduced
- Security/claims: Naomi Feldman — security language / compliance review
- Legal: Michael Grant (GC), Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel) — release forms, redlines, escalation

Target design partners (current working set)
- Arcadia Health (Private/VPC; regulated)
- QuantaPay (Dedicated capacity; strict latency SLOs)
- NovaDocs (Hosted API + Optimize; cost/perf story)
- HelioSupport (reference-call candidate; support-agent streaming + fallback)
- VectorForge (reference-call candidate; structured output + tool calling)
- Backup candidates: Moonlake Insurance, GlassKite AI

Key deliverables (what gets shipped)
1) Program foundations
- Reference program playbook (eligibility criteria, routing rules, SLAs, governance)
- Intake form + routing rules (AE owner → CS approval → SE assist; auto reminders)
- Release workflow (quote/logo release + approval checklist)

2) Case study production
- Case study template pack (interview guide, metrics checklist, approval checklist)
- 3–5 public case studies (web + PDF) with validated metrics + measurement notes

3) Reference call operations
- Reference call prep one-pager (internal)
- Reference profile page/record in HubSpot: boundaries, approved talking points, cadence limits
- Scheduling cadence: agreed windows + fallback contact if champion is OOO

Milestones + timeline (8–10 weeks)
Note: dates are placeholders; actual sequencing depends on customer bandwidth + legal turnaround.

Week 1 (May 5–May 9): Program definition + templates
- Draft program charter + governance + eligibility criteria (Camila / Soojin)
- Lock legal workflow + release template v1 (Michael / Sofia)
- Confirm intake + routing requirements for HubSpot (Isabelle / Tyler)
- Confirm target list v1 and owners (Stephanie / Lukas / AEs + CS)
Outputs
- “v1 program brief” approved by CRO
- Draft templates in Drive
Dependencies
- Legal availability for template review

Week 2 (May 12–May 16): Outreach + setup
- Outreach sequences v1 for AE/CSM (Soojin / Ethan / AEs)
- HubSpot fields spec + automation plan (Isabelle)
- Case study page requirements to Eng/Design (Ben / Tessa)
Outputs
- Outreach sequences ready
- HubSpot spec ready (ENG-4978 input)
Dependencies
- Alignment with Sales leaders on which accounts get public ask vs ref-call-only

Week 3 (May 19–May 23): Customer recruitment + kickoff interviews
- Secure verbal “yes” from 3–5 customers to participate (AEs + CSMs)
- Schedule 60-min case study interviews + 30-min technical validation call (Ethan + Markus)
- Start metrics worksheet per customer (Sana / Logan / Simran)
Outputs
- Interview calendar locked for at least 2 customers
- Metrics worksheet drafted with owners
Risks
- Customer bandwidth, especially regulated accounts

Week 4 (May 26–May 30): Drafting sprint #1
- First narrative draft for 1–2 customers (Ethan)
- Architecture diagram draft (Markus / Simran)
- Collect “proof artifacts” (dashboards/screenshots/log extracts; keep internal) (CS + SE)
Outputs
- Draft case study doc for Arcadia + NovaDocs (target)
Dependencies
- Access to performance data sources

Week 5 (Jun 2–Jun 6): Metrics validation gate
- Validate baselines + windows + workload definition (Sana / Logan / Simran)
- Resolve any benchmark anomalies/tickets BEFORE publishing numbers (SE + Eng as needed)
- Create “Claims register” section per case study (Soojin)
Outputs
- Metrics sign-off for 1–2 stories (internal)
- List of claims + allowed phrasing
Risks
- Regression during benchmark window forces re-run and delays

Week 6 (Jun 9–Jun 13): Customer review round #1 + legal starts
- Send draft + claims register to customer for redlines (AE/CSM + Ethan)
- Start release form redlines early (do not wait for final design) (Sofia / Michael)
- Security review on what can be public (Naomi + customer security contact)
Outputs
- Customer comments received for 1+ story
- Release negotiation in progress
Dependencies
- Customer approval chain clarity (who signs what)

Week 7 (Jun 16–Jun 20): Design + web staging
- PDF template + web components ready (Tessa / Ben)
- Create staging pages (Ben + Eng)
- Incorporate customer edits + tighten claims language (Ethan / Soojin)
Outputs
- Staging web page for 1 story + draft PDF
Dependencies
- DES-214 and ENG-4921 timelines

Week 8 (Jun 23–Jun 27): Final approvals (customer + legal)
- Final text lock + final proofread (Marketing)
- Customer sign-off captured in email + release form executed (Legal + AE)
- Confirm logo usage scope + quote attribution details (Soojin)
Outputs
- At least 1 story “approved to publish”
Risks
- Legal redlines extend beyond 2 weeks

Week 9 (Jun 30–Jul 4): Publish + enablement rollout
- Publish web + PDF (Ben)
- Update sales enablement: talk track, discovery Qs, objection snippets (Soojin)
- Announce internal launch: how to request a reference + where assets live (Camila / Tyler)
Outputs
- 1–2 case studies live
- Reference request process live

Week 10 (Jul 7–Jul 11): Reference call ops go-live + retrospective
- Intake form used for real reference requests; track SLA and outcomes (Rachel / Isabelle)
- Retro: what broke (legal, scheduling, claims) and update playbook (Camila)
- Report initial impact: influenced opps + call counts (Jordan wants a readout) (Isabelle)
Outputs
- Retro notes + v1.1 playbook updates

Gating criteria (must pass before we publish)
- Metrics validation completed
  - Measurement window dates documented
  - Baseline definition documented (what system / model / infra was used)
  - Workload described at a safe level (no sensitive traffic descriptions)
  - Validation owner named (SE/telemetry)
- Customer approvals complete
  - Final text approval
  - Approved quotes list + attribution
  - Logo usage rights confirmed
- Legal complete
  - Release executed (or approved alternative)
  - NDA constraints reviewed (esp. regulated)
- Security/claims review complete
  - No disallowed architecture/security details
  - “No overpromises” check

Weekly checklist (operating cadence)
Mon
- Review target list status + next steps (Camila / Tyler / AEs / CS)
- Identify blockers needing exec/legal support
Tue/Wed
- Interviews + technical validation calls
- Draft updates + claims register updates
Thu
- Approval workflow check (who’s holding what: customer, legal, security)
- HubSpot hygiene: reference readiness fields updated
Fri
- Publish readiness review (what can ship next week)
- Risk log update + mitigations

Dependencies (by workstream)
Legal
- Release form template finalized (prevents per-customer bespoke negotiation)
- Clear escalation rule: GC review required for regulated customers or custom withdrawal clauses
Design/Web
- Case study landing page + PDF template (DES-214)
- Docs/site “Case Studies” section nav + SEO basics (ENG-4921)
RevOps/CRM
- Reference readiness + approval status fields in HubSpot + automation/reminders (ENG-4978)
- Intake form routing rules + ownership logic (PM-701)
Content
- Messaging framework for production economics proof points (Soojin)
- Metrics worksheet + notes section requirements (Sana)

Risk log (draft)
1) Legal delays (release form redlines, logo rights scope)
- Likelihood: High
- Impact: High
- Mitigation:
  - Start release process as soon as customer agrees in principle
  - Offer tiered options: (a) logo + quote + named metrics, (b) logo + anonymized metrics, (c) anonymized story + no logo
  - Pre-approved alternate language for withdrawal clauses
  - Escalation to Michael if turnaround > 5 business days or customer adds non-standard publicity restrictions

2) Metrics disputes / inability to validate
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: High
- Mitigation:
  - Require a named validation owner per metric
  - Use conservative phrasing (“observed in a production workload over X weeks”)
  - If metric can’t be validated, remove it (do not substitute with soft language)

3) Customer bandwidth / champion churn
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: High
- Mitigation:
  - Confirm secondary contact + exec sponsor early
  - Keep asks small: 60-min interview + 1 review pass + 1 final sign-off
  - Offer opt-in to reference calls without public case study

4) Security review concerns block architecture detail
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: Medium
- Mitigation:
  - Provide “safe diagram” template (system-level, no network topology)
  - Avoid naming internal tools/vendors unless customer requests
  - Pre-review with Naomi before sending to customer security

5) Draft quality / inconsistency across stories
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: Medium
- Mitigation:
  - Use a single template + “claims register” standard
  - Soojin final copy pass for positioning and claim phrasing

6) Internal coordination overhead (AE/CS/Marketing/Legal)
- Likelihood: Medium
- Impact: Medium
- Mitigation:
  - One intake path only (HubSpot form) — no side-channel requests
  - Publish a single “source of truth” status tracker

Open questions (as of 2025-06-20)
- Reference call SLA: do we commit to scheduling within 5 business days or 7?
- Max reference call frequency per customer: 1/month default? (CS preference) How to enforce?
- Do we need an anonymized case study option as default for regulated accounts (Arcadia-style) vs pushing for public logo?
- Who owns final go/no-go for publishing metrics (Camila vs Jordan vs joint)?
- What qualifies as “influenced pipeline” in reporting (touchpoint definition in HubSpot)?

Notes to self (Camila)
- Keep QuantaPay story honest: if benchmark window had a regression, include caveats or wait.
- Make sure we don’t publish anything that implies data retention beyond what we actually offer (Arcadia is very sensitive here).
- Need internal FAQ for Sales: what to say when a prospect asks “can I talk to a customer in my industry?”
